subject: Unexpected cross-account token charges after key rotation
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cloudly.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, billing@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@cloudly.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected cross-account charges after key rotation

Hi Lauren / Redwood Billing,

We're seeing a large unexpected spike on our August invoice that appears attributed to both our legacy project (cloudly-ingest-prod) and the new tenant (cloudly-eu). We rotated API keys on Aug 5 as part of the migration but the usage split in the CSV export looks duplicated for many request IDs.

Quick facts:
- Export attached (usage_export_20260801-20260827.csv) with rows showing same request_id across two account ids
- Approx $24,500 in unexpected extra charges on the EU billing line (invoice #CLD-0826)
- Cloudly AI GmbH (DE) is VAT-registered; we need VAT-corrected invoicing for EU entity

We need: a breakdown of which account each request actually belonged to, a proposal for a corrective credit, and confirmation on how VAT will be handled for any retroactive adjustment. We are putting this on invoice hold until resolved.

Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Ops
Cloudly AI GmbH

- Marcus to run a short attribution audit against raw ingestion logs and the rotation audit.
- Ben to propose a provisional credit while we validate (so you don't get blocked on cashflow).

Can you attach the HubSpot invoice/PO number or the tax ID for Cloudly GmbH so our billing team can prep VAT-compliant docs? Also confirm whether you want the correction applied to the EU invoice or as a standalone credit note.

I’ll follow up within 24 business hours with an ETA.

—Lauren

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cloudly.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected cross-account charges after key rotation

Hi Alex — thanks for the fast follow. We dug into an initial sampling overnight. High-level summary:

- Root cause hypothesis: during the Aug 5 rotation window our ingestion layer continued accepting both old and new keys; a subset of proxies applied a permissive prefix-match that caused requests signed with the rotated key to be attributed to both the old project and the new EU tenant for ~48 hours.
- Impact window: Aug 5 02:14 UTC -> Aug 7 02:11 UTC (approx)
- Duplicate-attributed tokens (per our sample) appear concentrated in long-chat sessions and streaming sessions where request batching coalesced IDs.

Proposed commercial remediation:
1) Provisional credit: we can issue a provisional credit of $12,500 to Cloudly AI GmbH immediately to offset cashflow while we finish the audit.
2) Final split: once Marcus confirms exact counts, we propose splitting the duplicated charges proportionally by true-request ownership. Based on sampling we expect the final credit to be in the $20–26k range (so $12.5k provisional is conservative).
3) VAT handling: we will issue corrected invoices and credit notes to Cloudly AI GmbH and include VAT breakdowns. If you prefer a standalone credit note (easier for accounting), we can do that and provide VAT-corrected invoices for any remaining balance.

Please confirm acceptance of the provisional credit and whether you want the correction applied to the EU invoice (preferred for bookkeeping) or as a separate credit. I’ve attached a draft credit note stub (proposed_credit_note.pdf).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, Alex Chen <alex.chen@cloudly.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected cross-account charges after key rotation

Alex / team — I pulled the raw ingestion events and the rotation audit. Attaching a short extract (rotation_audit_log_excerpt.txt and raw-usage-ids.txt). Notes:

- Confirmed duplicate mapping: request_id sample lines 5–47 show identical request_id and signature hash present in both account buckets on Aug 5 02:25–03:10 UTC.
- Code path: a backward-compatible prefix compare we shipped to handle key-format variance — edge case allowed overlapping keys where the shorter key was a prefix of the newer key. The check should have used an exact match.
- Fix deployed: Aug 7 03:00 UTC — exact-match enforcement and a backfill job to reapply attribution corrected ~92% of affected rows.
- Outstanding: ~8% of rows require manual resolution because they were processed in a concatenated batch and lack unique routing metadata; these are the ones driving the $20–26k estimate.

I recommend: accept Ben’s provisional credit, we’ll finish the manual sweep and provide the final CSV with per-request corrected account_id and an MD5 checksum so you can reconcile locally. ETA for final CSV: 48 hours.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Billing Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the patience and for providing your VAT ID. Glad Marcus could validate the root cause and timeframe.

Next steps (agreed):
- We will issue the provisional credit of $12,500 to Cloudly AI GmbH within 24 hours (applied to invoice CLD-0826 as a credit note).
- Marcus will deliver the final per-request CSV and reconciliation checksums within 48 hours.
- After reconciliation we will issue corrected invoices / final credit note. If the final adjustment differs from the provisional amount, we will either bill or credit the delta and provide VAT-compliant invoice/credit documents.
- Accounting needs your confirmation that Cloudly AI GmbH (DE123456789) is the invoice entity. If yes, no further action required. If not, please send the invoicing entity name and VAT ID.

I’ll keep this thread open until the final CSV and documents are posted. Thanks again — we’ll get this closed quickly.

—Lauren
